A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAS/CURE research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including identifying substantive protocol differences.

before.justification: Section 6 and Tables 2–4 report original synthetic simulations and analyses of Amazon reviews and Galaxy Zoo images.

after.justification: Section 7 and Tables 2–3 retain original empirical results and add UniPT/UniPAS comparisons. Appendix E.5 reports an additional labeled-data sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: V2 retains PAS but introduces UniPT and UniPAS for unknown second moments (Section 6, Appendix C). UniPT estimates one shared, clipped power-tuning parameter; UniPAS adds pooled-moment shrinkage weights and a modified risk criterion. These are new procedures beyond v1's existing sample-moment implementation of PAS.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic model, Amazon Fine Food Reviews and Galaxy Zoo 2 for compound mean estimation, with the same predictors. Galaxy regrouping and varying labeled-data fractions revise protocols within this retained dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 3 adds UniPT and UniPAS to the real-world comparisons while retaining all six original baselines. The synthetic comparison set is unchanged. StratPPI receives additional discussion but is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds experiments varying the labeled fraction from 1% to 40%, beyond the retained 20/80 main setting. Galaxy grouping changes from 122 REDSHIFT_SIMPLE_BIN groups to 100 WVT_BIN groups (v1 Appendix D.4; v2 Appendix E.3). This is a substantive reported protocol revision, although identical retained table values do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E.5 and Figure 6 add a substantial sensitivity analysis of labeled-data availability across both datasets and both Amazon predictors. Existing stage ablations remain, but v1's Figure 4 analysis comparing individual PAS/PT estimates against pseudo-ground truth is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 200 replicates and table results with one standard error. The real-data uncertainty calculation and its restriction to randomness from labeled/unlabeled splitting are retained (v1 Appendix D.5; v2 Appendix E.4). No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Every shared numerical table entry, including standard errors, is unchanged. V2 adds UniPT/UniPAS results and Figure 6's ratio-dependent MSE curves; for example, Amazon-base UniPAS reports 8.879 ± 0.073 versus retained PAS 8.517 ± 0.071, in units of 10^-3. V1's per-problem Figure 4 results disappear. Unchanged Galaxy scores accompany different stated grouping conditions, preventing a same-setting performance interpretation.

T1.justification: The original CURE and PAS guarantees remain. V2 adds global-tuning derivations, bounded-sample and nondegeneracy assumptions, UniPT consistency and variance-optimality statements, and UniPAS risk-consistency and optimality statements (Appendix C). Appendices F.5–F.7 supply new supporting proof arguments absent from v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: combining PPI with empirical Bayes, tuning shrinkage through CURE, asymptotic optimality and empirical estimation benefits. Additional variants and evidence do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges that practical plug-in PAS is outside the original known-moment theory, explains UniPAS's weaker oracle comparison, and distinguishes asymptotic consistency from finite-sample unbiasedness (Section 6, Appendix C.3). New Appendix A.2 substantially develops explanations of information sharing, predictor quality and the limits of the Bayesian analogy.

D1.justification: V2 adds UniPAS pseudocode, clarifies pooled centering in sample-moment formulas and revises Galaxy preprocessing instructions. Hardware, training times and code access remain unchanged, while the explicit BERT checkpoint revision edd66ab is omitted. Algorithm 2's final shrinkage weight conflicts with the definition in Appendix C.3, limiting reproducibility of the addition.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially expands positioning against StratPPI and multivariate PPI++, distinguishing estimands and asymptotic regimes and connecting global tuning to PPI++. V2 also adds relevant works including Egami, Fogliato, Ghosh and Gronsbell, and removes Tyser et al. Publication updates to existing references are not additional works.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the appendices around connections and intuition, unknown moments, baselines, experiments and finally proofs. It adds extensive explanatory subsections, a dedicated main-text section on unknown moments, acknowledgments and an impact statement. Much of the original main-text wording remains.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column draft to a two-column conference layout. V1 Tables 3–4 merge into an expanded v2 Table 3. The original Figure 4 scatterplots are removed; new ratio-sensitivity panels, a proof diagram and UniPAS pseudocode are added. Retained displays are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The new variants target v1's important known-moment limitation, while expanded explanations and label-budget experiments add value. However, v2's UniPT definition and Algorithm 2 disagree on the correction sign, and Algorithm 2 uses the global shrinkage parameter instead of the defined local weights. Galaxy scores also remain identical despite changed stated strata. These unresolved inconsistencies limit confidence in the new procedures and evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
